definition: A +2-card bonus to everyone's Harvest total that is applied when the Agekeeper rolls the same sign for the Cosmic Age as for their Zodiac Sign.
The two requirements on each Active Crucible Card that must be satisfied before a Stone can be Fired: an Alignment condition and a card set condition. Both must be met simultaneously.
Scores generated by comparing a player's Aspects against the Opposition Age. Calculated using the Harvest Bonus Scoring table and used to determine the outcome of Oppositions and Gambits.

The three-part identity of a Cosmic Age or Alignment source: Sign, Planet, and Element. Each Aspect can generate Bonus Cards in Harvest and Alignment Points in Opposition. Only the highest-matching Aspect per source counts.
A permanent structure built on the Zodiac Wheel. Each grants an ongoing Alignment source (Sign, Planet, Element) and two additional benefits. Only one player may build on any given Sign.

An automatic bonus that's awarded to a Defender who wins an Opposition. Each successive win against different Challengers in the same round grants the Defender +1 cumulative Alignment Points for all further Oppositions that round.

Groups of cards organized by Rank and Suit, following poker-hand conventions (pairs, three of a kind, straights, flushes, and so on). Assembled in a player's Spread to satisfy Alchemical Formulas on Crucible Cards.

A bonus token earned from a successful Offering to the Age. Grants 2-for-1 Reagent refining in the Cauldron, it is placed in for the full following round. Only one Catalyst may be active per Cauldron at a time.
One complete round of play, defined by the Zodiac Sign rolled by the Agekeeper in Spring. Its three Aspects govern Harvest bonuses, Alignment scoring, and the active Cosmic Effect for that round.
The unique game modifier is activated by the rolled Cosmic Age Sign. Applies to the entire round and affects all players. See the Cosmic Ages & Effects table in the Reference Appendix.

A player's personal set of four Crucible Cards, one per Stage of Transmutation (I–IV). Each card must be activated and its Alchemical Formula satisfied before the corresponding Stone stage can advance.
A Winter action in which a player bets cards on which Sign will rule the next Cosmic Age. A correct prediction doubles the wager; an incorrect one forfeits all wagered cards to the Fates.
The four board positions (1, 3, 5, 7) on the Transmutation Path, where a Stone undergoes active advancement. A Stone in the Forge is in a Forging state and is vulnerable to Opposition.
The state of a Philosopher's Stone when it occupies a Forge position. The Stone's Crucible Card is Fired (face-up, sideways), and the Stone may be targeted by Opposition.
A Summer action to seize a rival's Active Crucible Card by demonstrating your Spread satisfies its Alignment, at the cost of surrendering one of your own Active Crucible Cards.
The card-drawing phase of Spring. Each player receives 2 Base Harvest cards plus Bonus Cards determined by their Aspect Alignments with the current Cosmic Age.
The four safe positions (0, 2, 4, 6) on the Transmutation Path between Forge stages. A Stone resting on the Mantle Ring cannot be targeted by Opposition.

A collective Winter action in which players contribute Aligned cards toward a shared RP Threshold. If the Threshold is met, every contributing player receives a Cauldron Catalyst for the following round.
An Alignment contest declared in Phase 3: Autumn against a rival whose Stone is currently Forging. Alignment Points are compared; a Challenger victory sends the Defender's Stone to Stasis.
The Cosmic Age Sign in effect at the moment an Opposition is declared. All Alignment Points in that contest are scored against this Sign's Aspects.

A Reagent placed on the shield symbol beside a Forging Stone or Active Crucible Card. Acts as a mandatory entry cost that any Challenger must pay before declaring Opposition or a Gambit against that position.
The numerical value of a card is based on its Rank. Used to meet Cauldron Thresholds when refining Reagents. Numbered cards equal their face value; court cards carry higher fixed values.
The frozen state of a Philosopher's Stone after losing an Opposition. A Stone in Stasis cannot Temper or take Stone actions until the following Autumn, when it may attempt to return to the Forge.
The Autumn action of advancing a Stone that has completed a full round of Forging. The Stone moves from the Forge to the next Mantle Ring position, and its Crucible Card is discarded.
Definition
The overarching process of advancing the Philosopher's Stone from its starting position through all four Forge stages to the Altar of Kismeta. Completing Transmutation wins the game.
